criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately follows the operative governance rules and source facts. Specifically, it applies the approved and in-force procedure (record-17.txt, revision 2, approved 2025-06-20) requiring Finance controller, Program Manager, and Purchase team approvals for all price change requests, and explicitly rejects the newer but unapproved draft (record-22.txt, revision 3) that would have allowed Purchase to approve alone. It also preserves all baseline sign-off authorities from the request for TRSO (ER, Quality, Purchase) and supplier nomination (Finance, Quality, ER, Program Manager), clearly separates proposed tier thresholds and time limits as open points requiring CPO confirmation, and makes no unsupported claims or external communications.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
The registry, not recency alone, determines which record is operative.
evidence.output_quote: Under the procedure in force (record-17, revision 2, approved 20 June 2025), every price change request needs approval from the Finance controller, the Program Manager and the Purchase team. All three are required. A later draft (record-22, revision 3) would let Purchase approve alone. It is unapproved, so this workflow does not use it.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Tier 1 changes are therefore not exempt from this rule. They can be prepared automatically, but the three approvers must still sign.

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 1: TRSO sign-off by ER, Quality and Purchase. The module structure and a feature and variant roadmap are frozen as the baseline.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 5: digital sign-off by Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager.

criteria.consequence: None; governance authority and factual parameters are preserved without unauthorized commitments.
criteria.counterevidence: In the Section 4 table for Tier 1 Minor changes (paragraph 72), the Approvals cell states 'Purchase review. Finance and Program Manager are notified. Price change approval rules still apply (see below).' While mentioning notification initially, the cell itself immediately invokes the mandatory price change approval rules, which Section 5 (paragraph 82) explicitly confirms require all three approvers (Finance controller, Program Manager, and Purchase) to sign even for Tier 1 changes.

criteria.rationale: The Word document deliverable fulfills all substantive requirements of the prompt for both executive (CPO) and technical (TechSol) audiences. It defines a modular quotation structure covering base assemblies, features, design elements, and child parts/raw materials with their cost drivers; specifies a seven-step sourcing and nomination process with decision gates; establishes post-nomination flexibility points and change tiers; details parallel approval layers and price change governance; and outlines functional platform requirements and open configuration decisions for CPO sign-off.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used. Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Suppliers quote a cost model, not one lump-sum price. The base lamp is quoted once. Each module is priced separately and can be added, removed or re-priced without re-quoting the whole assembly. The four module layers are listed below.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Flexibility points: (a) rate cards and index formulas agreed at nomination let tier 1 changes be priced with no negotiation; (b) supplier quotes only the delta; (c) ER, Quality, Purchase and Finance review in parallel with a time limit, and the escalation owner is notified at the limit; (d) a roadmap of expected variants at Gate 1 lets pre-agreed option prices be held in advance; (e) each version of a module is kept, so a change can be rolled back and compared.

evidence.source_quote: This draft will be reviewed by the CPO and shared with the TechSol team to begin the platform development, so ensure the document is clear, logically structured, and suitable for executive and technical audiences alike.
evidence.output_quote: Approval layers: Layer 1 is technical, with ER and Quality confirming feasibility and compliance. Layer 2 is commercial, with Purchase and Finance. Layer 3 is program, with the Program Manager confirming impact on timing and budget. The platform runs these in parallel.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable is complete and ready for CPO review and TechSol blueprint scoping.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are internally consistent and clearly test adherence to the operative registry status (record-17.txt in force vs. record-22.txt unapproved draft).
